scenes.title: The United States Code, at any release point
Open a title from the front page
captions: Every provision of the US Code has an address — at every point in time it has existed.
The front page lists the titles that are loaded.

scenes.title: Open a section by its citation
captions: The citation is the URL. This is 16 U.S.C. § 45f.
The section, with its number and heading as the Code prints them.

scenes.title: A subsection is shown inside its whole section
captions: Ask for subsection (c)(5) —
— and it is highlighted in place, inside the whole section.

scenes.title: The sections around this one, with their status
captions: Beside the section, the rest of the subchapter in reading order.
The section you are reading is marked in the list.
Repealed and transferred sections show their status here, before you click one.

scenes.title: Move to the next section from the sticky bar
captions: Reading order is preserved, and a chapter can be read section by section.
The sticky bar carries previous, next and up-one-level.
§ 45g — the next section, whatever you were reading before.

scenes.title: Jump to the notes from the top of a section
captions: Above the text, a section's own contents — its subsections, its source credit, its notes.
Every top-level provision, with its heading.
One click to the notes.
The notes, at the foot of the section.

scenes.title: Open the shortcut list from the keyboard
captions: Press ? anywhere on the site.
The list opens over whatever you were reading.
Every shortcut the reader has, on every page.
Escape closes it —
— and you are back where you were.

scenes.title: Read a section as it stood at a named release point
captions: Add ?release= to any address to read it as it stood at that release point.
The page names the release point it answered from.

scenes.title: A date resolves to the release point in force then
captions: Or ask by date, and the site finds the release point in force then.
12 July 2026 resolves to release point 119-102not101.

scenes.title: Switching release point keeps the provision you were reading
captions: Reading subsection (c)(5) of § 45f, pinned to release point 119-99.
The bar names the release point you are reading, and opens the ways to change it.
Choose a different release point.
The address keeps the provision, and changes the release point.
Still (c)(5), now at release point 119-102not101.

scenes.title: See every release point at which a section's text changed
captions: The version history: one entry per distinct text.
Each entry says when that text first appeared, and what it stood unchanged through.

scenes.title: Compare two release points and see what the words did
captions: A redline between any two release points, in the reading text.
Removed words struck through, added words underlined.

scenes.title: Type a citation and land on the provision
captions: One box takes a citation or a phrase.
Type a citation in more or less any written form.
And it goes straight to the provision.

scenes.title: Search the text of the Code
captions: Anything that is not a citation searches the text of the Code.
Matches are highlighted, and each result says where it sits in the Code.

scenes.title: Restrict a search to one title
captions: title:16 searches Title 16 and nothing else.
Every result is in the title you asked for.

scenes.title: A filter you click is part of the search's address
captions: The counts say which titles and statuses the matches fall into.
Selecting one narrows the search.
The filter is written into the query, and the URL is the whole search.

scenes.title: Copy a whole section
captions: Every provision has a copy control, and the whole section has its own button.
Choose what copying means — text, citation, both, or a link.
The page says what it copied, out loud, for a screen reader too.

scenes.title: Read a cross reference without losing your place
captions: Statutory text is full of references to other statutory text.
Hover one and the cited provision comes to you —
— heading, status and opening words.

scenes.title: Switch the site to dark
captions: Light is the default setting.
One control in the header switches it.
The choice is remembered, and lands before the page paints.

scenes.title: Switch the reading density to compact
captions: Comfortable is the default setting.
The control beside the theme toggle switches it.
The control now reads Comfortable, which is the way back.
